Key Research Thinking Patterns: High-throughput functional genomics: Utilizing Random Barcode Transposon Sequencing (RB-TnSeq) to systematically map gene essentiality and conditional phenotypes across hundreds of metabolic and stress conditions in model organisms like Desulfovibrio vulgaris.

Multi-modal environmental validation: Combining field sampling with laboratory microcosms and genomic/phenotypic analysis to assess the specificity of diagnostic tools, such as identifying false positives in Enterolert assays caused by non-fecal bacteria like Paenibacillus.

Real-time molecular surveillance: Implementing allele-specific RT-qPCR and digital PCR to detect and track SARS-CoV-2 variants (e.g., Omicron) in wastewater, providing lead-time detection of community transmission trends before clinical reporting.

Statistical epidemiological modeling: Applying generalized linear modeling and time-series analysis to correlate wastewater pathogen concentrations with human disease incidence, seasonal patterns, and demographic factors to establish robust early warning thresholds.
Summary Description: Kara B. De León is an environmental microbiologist and epidemiologist specializing in wastewater-based surveillance and microbial physiology. Her research bridges fundamental microbial genetics, using RB-TnSeq to define metabolic networks in sulfate-reducing bacteria, with applied public health solutions. She develops and validates molecular diagnostic tools for monitoring fecal indicators and emerging pathogens, including SARS-CoV-2 variants and bacterial enterics, in wastewater systems. By integrating high-throughput sequencing, qPCR, and advanced statistical modeling, her work provides real-time early warning systems for disease outbreaks and antimicrobial resistance, directly informing public health policy and water quality management.
